examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Comparison sorting has an Ω(n log n) worst-case lower bound for arbitrary distinct keys. Stability preserves order among equal keys. Bubble-sort adjacent swaps equal inversion count. A merge is void when max(left)≤min(right), even if the input's other subarrays are unsorted.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
How many inversions does [4,1,3,2] contain?

**Answer: 4.** The inverted pairs are (4,1),(4,3),(4,2),(3,2). There are four. Any sorting process using only adjacent swaps must remove all four inversions.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Counting/radix sorting bypass the comparison lower bound by using assumptions about value range or representation.

“In-place” and “stable” are independent properties.
